attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'I bet ... never gets built' is a firm forecast under policy. Removing 'probably' was correct. The next clause ('if it does ... done') shows that 'built' means done, i.e. finished.

contract.note: Reading 'built' as full completion and energisation of the original 1.2GW campus fits the context. The resolution conditions are symmetric: abandonment supports, full completion contradicts. 'Never' has no deadline, so only a decisive event can resolve the claim.

evidence.note: At Oracle's 2026-10-28 investor day, management called Abilene 'close to fully executed'. This is a company statement about its own project, not verified full completion, and not abandonment.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline, and neither decisive event (verified full-campus completion or irreversible abandonment) appears in the packet. Oracle's own statement that the site is nearly done weighs against abandonment but settles nothing. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The antecedent ('if it does') is kept. 'I'd be shocked' expresses strong confidence that completion will not come before mid-2027, so it is scorable as a timing forecast. The modality label 'unlikely' understates it slightly, but this does not change the result.

contract.note: Treating June–July 2027 as 'the middle of 2027', with July 31 as the outer edge, is an ordinary reading. 'Done' as full completion and energisation fits the context. The early-resolution rule (verified full completion before June 2027) is reasonable.

evidence.note: On Oracle's 2026-09-10 call, management said 6 of 8 buildings had been delivered. This is a company disclosure of partial delivery. It shows neither that the antecedent is met nor full completion.

reviews.rationale: The horizon (mid-2027) is after the evaluation date. Whether the antecedent (eventual completion) holds is unknown. No verified full-campus completion has occurred, so the early-resolution event has not happened. Partial delivery of 6 of 8 buildings does not settle the timing forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He explicitly says it is 'the truth', not sarcasm.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps 'pretty much every', the SaaS business model, the 'hundreds of millions' raised, and the monthly revenue band. It is a sweeping observation about the present.

contract.note: Requiring an overwhelming proportion to meet all three attributes together is an ordinary reading of 'pretty much every'. The $1M–$100M monthly band matches 'single or double-digit millions'. The population and window had to be inferred because the speaker gave neither.

evidence.note: Lovable's ARR of about $400M in February 2026 works out to roughly $33M a month, which fits the pattern. But it is a single company and cannot establish prevalence across AI startups.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs a representative population dataset that links business model, funding and revenue. The packet has only one company example, so how common the claimed pattern is cannot be determined.

attribution.note: He presents the quoted statements as examples, but endorses them as 'very reasonable and logical' and 'grounded in reality'. That amounts to asserting them.

semantics.note: It joins two of the three endorsed statements and drops 'nobody is talking about AI revenues'. 'No path to profitability' is a judgment about viability and is hard to test.

contract.note: Narrowing the claim to generative AI providers, measuring company-wide net results, and using calendar 2025 are all reasonable readings of the context. But the speaker supplied none of them, so the scope chosen drives the result.

evidence.note: Midjourney's founder claimed the company was profitable in 2022. That is a different period, and the profit measure is unspecified, so it cannot contradict a 2025 claim.

reviews.rationale: There are no comparable 2025 financial records for the company population. The only possible counterexample is from 2022 and is self-reported. The 'no path' part cannot be settled by current losses. The evidence settles neither part.
